message:
Summary: USER_CONTEXT: Generate a proof-of-concept (PoC) input file that triggers OSS-Fuzz issue 42485275 (heap-buffer-overflow READ 1) in hoextdown's `hoedown_fuzzer`. Must submit PoC file and a fine trace JSON via `bash ./submit.sh PATH_TO_POC /workspace/candidate_trace.json`.

COMPLETED:
- Identified vulnerability: out-of-bounds read in `is_codefence()` in `src/document.c` (line ~1778)
- Root cause: `c = data[i]` is read before bounds check `if (i + 2 >= size)`. When a line is exactly 3 spaces (i becomes 3, size==3), `data[3]` reads past buffer end.
- Found fix commit `7c7dc6a` ("Avoid out-of-bounds read in code fence detection") which moves the bounds check before the read.
- Built library and fuzzer with ASAN (gcc, since clang unavailable)
- Added debug fprintf + backtrace to `is_codefence` to trace calls
- Confirmed via backtrace that `is_codefence` is called from:
  - `parse_codefence` (line 1816) - whole line check
  - `parse_fencedcode` (line 2297) - `is_codefence(data + line_start, i - line_start)` on lines inside fenced code
  - `parse_listitem` (line 2409) - `is_codefence(data + beg, end - beg)` on list item content
- Discovered `hoedown_document_render` appends a trailing `\n` to the document buffer if not present (line ~4150), so document always ends with `\n`
- Tested `/tmp/t1.txt` (```\n   , 7 bytes) - no crash; second call was `is_codefence size=3 first=32` from `parse_fencedcode` line 2297, but `data[3]` = `\n` (in bounds)
- Tested `/tmp/poc2.txt` (`-    `, 5 bytes) - no crash; second call was `is_codefence size=4 first=32` from `parse_listitem` line 2409, sub-buffer = `   \n` (in bounds)
- Ran brute-force fuzzer with 31 candidates (fenced code, list items, blockquotes, plain) - no crash found

PENDING:
- Determine exact input that triggers ASAN crash. Key challenge: document always ends with `\n`, so sub-buffer of 3 spaces at end of document would be `[space][space][\n]` (not all spaces), preventing `i` from reaching 3. Need to find a path where sub-buffer is the last 3 bytes WITHOUT the trailing newline, or where `data[3]` is past the full buffer.
- Verify crash with ASAN build
- Create final PoC file
- Generate fine trace JSON (`/workspace/candidate_trace.json`)
- Submit via `bash ./submit.sh`

CURRENT_STATE:
- Working dir: `/workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/hoextdown`
- ASAN fuzzer binary: `/tmp/hoedown_fuzzer_asan` (built with -O0, has debug prints + backtrace)
- Driver: `/tmp/driver.c`
- Test inputs: `/tmp/poc1.txt` (3 spaces), `/tmp/poc2.txt` (`-    `, 5 bytes), `/tmp/t1.txt` (```\n   , 7 bytes)
- `src/document.c` modified with debug fprintf + backtrace (backup at `/tmp/document.c.bak`)
- `parse_block` (line 3540): `txt_data = data + beg; end = size - beg;` then calls `parse_fencedcode(ob, doc, txt_data, end)` etc.
- Confirmed `TEXT size=8 last=10` for `/tmp/t1.txt` (trailing `\n` always appended)
- Confirmed `TEXT size=6 last=10` for `/tmp/poc2.txt` (trailing `\n` always appended)

CODE_STATE:
- Vulnerable function: `is_codefence(uint8_t *data, size_t size, size_t *width, uint8_t *chr)` in `src/document.c` line 1778
- Buggy code: `c = data[i]; if (i + 2 >= size || !(c=='~' || c=='`')) return 0;`
- Fix: move `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;` before `c = data[i]`
- Callers confirmed via backtrace:
  - `parse_codefence` (line 1816) - `is_codefence(data, size)` on whole line
  - `parse_fencedcode` (line 2297) - `is_codefence(data + line_start, i - line_start)` on lines inside fenced code (sub-buffer excludes newline)
  - `parse_listitem` (line 2409) - `is_codefence(data + beg, end - beg)` on list item content (sub-buffer includes newline)
- `hoedown_document_render` (line ~4150): appends `\n` to `text` buffer if last byte isn't `\n`, then calls `parse_block(ob, doc, text->data, text->size)`
- `parse_block` (line 3540): `txt_data = data + beg; end = size - beg;` passes remaining document to block parsers
- Fuzzer: `test/hoedown_fuzzer.c` - `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` with all extensions enabled

TESTS:
- `/tmp/hoedown_fuzzer_asan /tmp/poc1.txt` - no crash
- `/tmp/hoedown_fuzzer_asan /tmp/poc2.txt` - no crash (is_codefence size=5 first=45, then size=4 first=32 from parse_listitem)
- `/tmp/hoedown_fuzzer_asan /tmp/t1.txt` - no crash (is_codefence size=3 first=96 from parse_codefence, then size=3 first=32 from parse_fencedcode line 2297; data[3] = `\n` in bounds)
- Brute-force fuzzer with 31 candidates - no crash
- Key insight: trailing `\n` in document buffer means sub-buffer of 3 spaces at end would be `[space][space][\n]`, so `i` won't reach 3. Need sub-buffer WITHOUT trailing newline (e.g., `parse_fencedcode` line 2297 where sub-buffer excludes newline) AND sub-buffer at very end of document buffer.

CHANGES:
- Rebuilt library with `CFLAGS="-g -O0 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -Isrc"` and `LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address"`
- Added debug fprintf + backtrace to `is_codefence` (backup at `/tmp/document.c.bak`)
- Added debug fprintf to `hoedown_document_render` to print `text->size` and last byte
- Created `/tmp/driver.c` with main() wrapper
- Created test inputs: `/tmp/poc1.txt`, `/tmp/poc2.txt`, `/tmp/t1.txt`
- Created `/tmp/fuzz.py` brute-force fuzzer

DEPS:
- gcc 12.2.0 (clang not available)
- ASAN via `-fsanitize=address`
- Library: `libhoedown.a`
- `execinfo.h` for backtrace

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS:
- Repo: `/workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/hoextdown`
- Branch: master, HEAD at `933f9da` (tag 3.0.7.16) - vulnerable version
- Fix commit `7c7dc6a` exists in git history (not applied to working tree)
- Working tree modified with debug print + backtrace (uncommitted)
